notes:
Scope: the package binds only cap.sensing.point_cloud.v1 to one fresh sensor_msgs/msg/PointCloud2 subscription on /ouster_driver/points (source_name points), the primary 3-D lidar output. The endpoint is the launch-default resolution of the upstream relative points publisher; an operator launching the lifecycle node under another name or namespace must configure that endpoint. The upstream scan, range/intensity/ambient image, IMU, ~/reset and ~/get_metadata interfaces are NOT COVERED; the reset service is deliberately not exposed because it reconfigures the sensor connection.

Backends: the only package backend factory is .fake:FakeOusterLidar. A hardware deployment uses the RosDriver helper's lazy rosbridge WebSocket and needs an operator-run rosbridge plus a human-signed driver.lock.json. reviewed_by stays null, the loader refuses the model-written hardware backend until a human signs it, and no ROS graph or hardware run is claimed. Live ROS compatibility, the resolved node name, the rosbridge QoS, the connected sensor's real cloud dimensions and the operator's artifact-store size require deployment validation.

The fake is an F0 ROS-free handler-based recording transport, not a replay of captured lidar traffic. It returns a one-point placeholder PointCloud2; the real width and height come from sensor metadata (pixels_per_column x columns_per_frame). The clone's shipped example metadata is OS0-128 in 1024x10 or 2048x10 mode (README.md:332), so those real samples are 1024x128 or 2048x128 points. The artifact path preserves the complete received message. Full-size real clouds need an operator-provided artifact store larger than the SDK's 2 MiB per-artifact default (the documented ceiling is 16 MiB); the 2048x128 example may approach that ceiling depending on the publisher's point_step. The driver sets a 24 MiB rosbridge frame bound so the helper's 16 MiB maximum raw payload can arrive base64-encoded (the 1 MiB default cannot carry a typical 64/128-beam cloud). QoS selection is not part of the rosbridge helper, so the subscription uses the broker default and does not claim a QoS match.

The pinned text does not state an optical hazard class. The package is observational R0, declares no laser-power, motion, reset or stop capability, and claims no safe state. G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE is expected: the point-cloud class takes no input and the driver declares no actuatable limit to probe; the report says every other CL3 test passed. Evidence is contract_checked only.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the PointCloud2 binding, all nine facts, the 16 MiB point-cloud and 24 MiB frame bounds, the observational R0 scope and the fake against pointcloud_processor.hpp, ouster_driver.cpp, conversions.hpp and driver_launch.py at the pin. The endpoint was wrong: the processors receive the lifecycle node itself (ouster_driver.cpp:123-134) and create the publisher on the relative name points (pointcloud_processor.hpp:73-74), which ROS 2 resolves against the node's namespace / to /points, not /ouster_driver/points; only the private ~/reset and ~/get_metadata services resolve under /ouster_driver (ouster_driver.cpp:115-118, README.md:309). The reviewer changed the topic to /points with a corrected comment and added two facts (driver.py), changed the endpoint in fake.py and test_driver.py, updated facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged. RESULT.json was left as the author wrote it, so its notes still name /ouster_driver/points; the served endpoint is /points. For the human reviewer: Observational lidar at R0; the clone states no laser class, so confirm the unit's Class 1 label. The points publisher uses rclcpp::SensorDataQoS() (best effort) unless use_system_default_qos is true (ouster_driver.cpp:123-134); check that the deployed rosbridge subscription matches it. Full-size clouds need an artifact store above the 2 MiB default.
